estimand: rank of the estimated beta matrix
scale_behavior: rank is invariant to nonsingular factor rescaling
threshold: rank must equal the number of priced factors using the numerical tolerance max(n_assets n_factors) times machine epsilon times the largest singular value
justification: the second pass cannot identify all risk prices if beta columns are linearly dependent

estimand: cross-sectional standard deviation of beta_i_rate times standard_deviation(rate innovation)
scale_behavior: invariant to rescaling of the rate factor
threshold: at least 0.10 times the cross-sectional standard deviation of beta_i_mkt times standard_deviation(market factor)
justification: compares dispersion in fitted-return units instead of raw beta units
failure_interpretation: the short-rate column has too little economically scaled cross-sectional variation

estimand: OLS spanning R-squared of the rate innovation on a constant plus the registered non-short-rate comparator factors available on the common intersection
scale_behavior: R-squared and the residual ratio are both scale free
threshold: pass when R2_span is at most 0.90 equivalently when s_span equal to sqrt(1 - R2_span) is at least sqrt(0.10) which is 0.31622776601683794; the R-squared form is authoritative and a numerical tolerance of 1e-12 is applied in the lenient direction to both forms because the computed residual ratio equals sqrt(1 - R2_span) only up to floating-point rounding
justification: a factor whose variation is more than 90 percent reproduced by the existing traded-factor set retains less than one tenth of its variance as independent identifying variation
failure_interpretation: the rate factor is redundant with the comparator factor set

estimand: the same spanning statistic computed against Mkt-RF alone
threshold: no threshold; reported next to the primary spanning statistic
justification: shows how much of the spanning result comes from the market factor alone

estimand: singular values and condition number of the beta matrix
threshold: no threshold because the condition number is the ratio of the largest to smallest singular value and duplicates the rank gate
justification: reported to describe conditioning without creating a redundant rejection rule

estimand: change in the rate-attributable fitted-premium spread after omitting each anomaly family
scale_behavior: uses fitted premium beta_i_rate times lambda_rate so it is factor-scale invariant
threshold: no sign reversal and no loss of materiality classification in any leave-one-family system
justification: prevents one anomaly family from driving the economic conclusion
failure_interpretation: the pricing interpretation is fragile to test-asset composition

estimand: maximum absolute standardized DFBETA of any portfolio on lambda_rate
threshold: maximum absolute standardized DFBETA must be below 1
justification: guards against a single portfolio determining the rate price
failure_interpretation: the result is influential and the pricing interpretation is fragile

estimand: 95 percent joint-bootstrap percentile interval for the rate-attributable fitted-premium spread
scale_behavior: uses fitted-return units and recomputes beta and lambda jointly in every draw
threshold: the interval must not contain both +0.25 and -0.25 monthly percentage points
justification: weak precision can make a significant risk price uninterpretable
failure_interpretation: the sign and economic magnitude of the fitted premium are too imprecise

scale_behavior: parameter scale changes with factor normalization but interpretation is reported through fitted premium
threshold: no standalone confirmatory threshold; reported with the fitted-premium bootstrap
justification: the article benchmark uses Shanken uncertainty for risk prices
failure_interpretation: asymptotic uncertainty is descriptive unless aligned with fitted-premium inference
